summary: Benton County hilltop: a 1930s crow's nest is listed; in 1942 a ground AWS post was approved instead of a tower; abandoned, crow's nest not located in 2024.

facts.design: 1942 AWS ground post (16x18 ground house used as living quarters, 10x12 storage building, woodshed); no tower for that use
facts.status_note: Abandoned; a crow's nest was reportedly still there in 1995 but was not located in 2024.

events.note: Source gives only the 1930s for a crow's nest; exact year unknown.
Buildings for an AWS ground post approved in August 1942; one listing calls the site an AWS cabin.
Activation date given as December 7, 1942, under the Eugene Filter Center.

corrections.why: The only height in the sources is an 80 to 100 foot tower discussed in 1942 for fire detection; the approved plan was a ground post, not a tower.

corrections.proposed: crow's nest (1930s listing); 1942 AWS ground post
corrections.why: Both listings type the site as a crow's nest, and the 1942 AWS building was a ground house.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com lists a 1930s crow's nest and a 1942 AWS cabin; the Oregon Lookouts page documents only a 1942 ground post and advises against a tower. Only one listing reports a crow's nest, so the 1930s structure is uncorroborated.

notes_for_editor: Two independent pages agree on the 1942 AWS ground post, but the 1930s crow's nest rests on one listing. Brief's location conflict is unresolved: FFLA directory 44.65623,-123.36243 (matches our record) vs west_us_lookouts 44.62817,-123.38739. The Oregon Lookouts page header says 10S-5W-29 while its 1942 letter places the post in Section 36, T10S R6W. The 1942 post is also called Price Observation Post (Albany 95) and Arboretum in planning letters. The Oregon Lookouts 1942 letters themselves document the AWS role. No staffing, access or current-site source found; access left unset. Status Removed on the weebly page is unexplained.
